requirements.text: The XS shall have the ability to redefine or reset names of connect descriptors to database server instances.
At a minimum, the session time-out values shall be user definable and be able to be reset prior to initialization of a user session.
The data management services shall support managing various types of data, database architectures and platforms that includes hardware and software at the specified sites.
The Registry shall provide standard APIs as specified in Appendix B .
The XS function shall provide standard APIs as specified in Appendix C .
The XS shall internally interface (transparent to the operator) with the existing data elements of the DBIF, DAC, and COTS RDBMS products.
The Registry software shall be portable and required to execute on COE-compliant platforms.
The XS software shall be delivered in accordance with DII COE guidelines.

Manager services shall implement role-based access control (RBAC) and maintain an immutable audit log of all administrative actions, including user creation, privilege escalation, and configuration changes.
The XS shall enforce Mandatory Access Control (MAC) and Discretionary Access Control (DAC) policies consistent with the DII COE security architecture for all XML metadata and data access operations.
Session time-out values shall be configurable within defined security policy bounds; the system shall terminate inactive sessions and require re-authentication upon expiration.
Define the failure domains and the impact of a failure in one segment on the availability of others.
Specify the default session time-out value and the allowable range (e.g., 30 seconds to 24 hours) to prevent misconfiguration.
Define the required data consistency model (e.g., ACID vs. BASE) and the expected recovery time objectives (RTO) for these platforms.
Define the specific COE-compliant operating environments and the required verification process for ensuring consistent behavior across these platforms.
Define specific latency and throughput targets for the data management services under defined low, medium, and high load scenarios.
Specify the maximum number of concurrent registry users, total registry entries, and expected query response time under peak load.
Define the specific network latency or packet loss thresholds that trigger a dynamic adjustment of session time-out values.
